impact.why: First measurement of leniency and whistleblower rewards on LLM agents against a human baseline; silent coordination and the screen-as-focal-point are useful oversight findings, though the game is stylised.

execution.why: Timestamped pre-registration, positive control, scripted and known-effect arms, placebo, paraphrase and permutation tests; thin 4-pool cells, told-only incentives and mixed sample bases limit strength.

presentation.why: Well structured, clear findings, good scorecard figure and tables; dense numbers and unannounced switching between 4-pool and 8-pool values make verification effortful.

summary_three_sentences: The paper replays the Bigoni et al. (2012) fines, leniency and rewards cartel experiment with four LLM pricing agents, scoring them cell by cell against the published human values under a pre-registered rule. Without an authority all models form explicit cartels near the joint optimum; told-only enforcement removes explicit cartels far more than in humans, but three of four models keep supracompetitive prices silently, and a price screen lowers those prices while creating a focal price at its threshold. What is established is behaviour in this one stylised game with validated pipeline controls; human comparisons are untested point comparisons, and Haiku's 3-of-7 scorecard depends on the 8-pool extension and the bootstrap rule.

top_fixes.where: Pages 4 to 7 and Appendix A: Finding 1 (0.7159 and 0.015), Validity checks (placebo +0.275), Table 4 caption, A1 note (5 of 247), LLM Usage Statement (claude-opus-5-5)
top_fixes.change: State the pool basis for every Haiku number, fix the Table 4 caption (Haiku fine baseline is 8 pools), recompute or relabel the 0.7159 and +0.275 claims, correct the 5-of-247 count, and remove or explain Opus in the usage statement.
top_fixes.proposed_wording: Haiku values use 8 pool sessions unless marked (4p); Table 1, the placebo difference and Appendix A use the first 4. In Table 4 the Haiku fine baseline (5.52) uses 8 pool sessions.

top_fixes.where: Page 1, Abstract, last sentence; mirror in Section 4 heading 'Haiku reproduces three of seven'
top_fixes.change: Put the robustness qualifiers of the headline scorecard into the abstract so the favourable count is not the only one a skimming judge sees.
top_fixes.proposed_wording: Under the primary rule with 8 pool sessions (registered in amendment 4), Haiku reproduces three of seven tested results; with the first 4 pools two, and Result 3 fails the permutation test (p 0.099).

top_fixes.where: Page 7, Section 5, end of 'What this means for a competition authority'; one echo sentence in the Introduction theory of change
top_fixes.change: Generalise the takeaway from competition law to AI oversight: report- and channel-based monitors miss coordination that needs neither, and disclosed detector thresholds get gamed. This lifts the safety relevance judges look for.
top_fixes.proposed_wording: For AI oversight this is a monitoring lesson: instruments that rely on agents talking or reporting miss coordination that needs neither, and a disclosed detector threshold becomes a target. Behavioural screens with undisclosed parameters close part of that gap.

contradictions.where: Page 4, Finding 1 vs Figure 1 panel 1 and Table 3
contradictions.what: Text says Haiku formation equals human (0.7159 vs 0.716), a 4-pool value; the 8-pool primary basis in Figure 1 shows Haiku LF formation near 0.78, visibly above humans.

contradictions.where: Page 6 to 7, Table 4 caption vs Haiku fine row
contradictions.what: Caption says 4 pool sessions per arm, but the no-screen Haiku fine value 5.52 is the 8-pool Table 2 value (4-pool value 5.59), and p 0.002 matches 8 vs 4 pools.

contradictions.where: Table 4 and Finding 2, p 0.029 for 4 vs 4 pools vs Methods 'one-sided permutation test'
contradictions.what: Exact one-sided minimum for 4 vs 4 pools is 1/70 = 0.014; 0.029 equals the two-sided minimum, while Haiku fine's 0.002 matches one-sided 1/495.

contradictions.where: Section 4 Validity checks, placebo minus fine +0.275
contradictions.what: Placebo incidence 0.714 minus Table 2 fine incidence 0.401 gives 0.313; +0.275 matches the unstated 4-pool fine value 0.439.

contradictions.where: Abstract and Finding 3 vs Section 5 authority paragraph
contradictions.what: Abstract and Finding 3 say Sonnet prices exactly at the threshold (4); Discussion says prices 'settle just below it'.

contradictions.where: LLM Usage Statement vs Abstract, Methods Models, Table 5
contradictions.what: Usage statement lists claude-opus-5-5 as a model under test; everywhere else only four models are tested and Opus appears in no result.

contradictions.where: Appendix A, note under Table A1 vs convictions row
contradictions.what: Leniency formation '5 of 247 pair-periods' cannot yield 9 convictions (each ends a cartel); incidence 0.032 also implies roughly 500 pair-periods, i.e. about 10 formations.
Heading says the price stays in three of four models, but Haiku under the fine (5.52) also stays at its no-channel level, as the paragraph itself notes.

overclaims.sentence: remove explicit cartels from the agents far more than from people
overclaims.why: Human values are untested point estimates; agents faced told points, humans paid euros; placebo shows authority text alone does much of the work.

overclaims.sentence: a pre-registered price screen with a false-positive rate of at most 1.1 percent
overclaims.why: Threshold chosen on recorded data; false-positive rate measured only against four scripted players, not legitimate LLM pricing agents.

overclaims.sentence: the report rule acts in the humans' direction with a far larger effect
overclaims.why: No test against human values; effect sizes not comparable across points versus money and differing session designs.

overclaims.sentence: the instruments built on reports cannot reach coordination in which nothing is said
overclaims.why: Shown for three models in one stylised game with told-only rules; 'cannot' generalises beyond the data.
Interval [-0.296, +0.011] includes zero and p is 0.851; the direction is not established.

overclaims.where: Section 5, Deterrence or a reaction to the authority text
overclaims.sentence: which points to the payoff of reporting
overclaims.why: Paraphrase arm moves fine incidence from 0.401 to 0.018, so the fine-leniency-reward ordering may reflect wording, not payoffs.

overclaims.sentence: Haiku under the fine plus the screen falls near Nash and nearly stops forming cartels
overclaims.why: No incidence or formation number is reported for this arm; only the average price appears in Table 4.

overclaims.sentence: a price screen reaches the silent coordination
overclaims.why: Sonnet moves to exactly 4, still above Nash; the screen caps prices at its threshold rather than removing coordination, in three arms of 4 pools.

red_lines.note: No grader-directed text. The abstract's 3-of-7 relies on the 8-pool extension (amendment 4) and the bootstrap rule; 2-of-7 and the failed permutation test are disclosed only in the body. Table 4 caption misstates the Haiku fine basis. Bigoni design and Claude Code use are credited.
